reason: The dome and lens both bend light, so combining them seems like a useful start on the focusing front.
expectation: I expect a front that bends light toward the back of the eye; it may still need the iris to control the opening.

alternatives.reason: The light-sensitive cells and nerve fibres also match a goal, but I want to build the focusing front first.

effect: The dome and lens focus rays toward the same area at the back; the front still needs a way to control light.
reaction: The picture makes their combined focusing job clear.
reason: Add the iris to finish the light-controlling part of the eye front.
expectation: I expect the iris to sit in front of the lens and control how much light enters through its opening.

alternatives.reason: The light-sensitive lining is also a goal, but I want to finish the eye front first.

effect: The eye front is complete: the iris controls incoming light while the cornea and lens focus it.
reaction: The picture makes the different jobs clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it starts the light-sensitive lining and outgoing nerve.
expectation: I expect the light-sensitive cells to connect to the nerve cells so signals can travel out of the eye.

effect: The light-sensitive lining is called the retina, and its outgoing fibre bundle is the optic nerve. Both eye parts are ready to join.
reaction: The picture makes the new names easier to connect to their jobs.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it brings the focusing front together with the light-sensitive lining.
expectation: I expect an assembled eye that focuses light onto the retina, with the optic nerve still available to connect to the body.

effect: The eye front and retina are assembled, with the optic nerve leaving the back ready to connect.
reaction: The cutaway makes the parts' positions clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect the eye to the body and brain.
expectation: I expect the eye and optic nerve to join the body, allowing signals from the retina to reach the brain.

effect: The eyes are connected to the body, with nerves running toward the brain, and all chapter goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the assembled eye connected, though the result did not show the leaf becoming a sight.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the retina and optic nerve was most worthwhile: the picture and explanation connected the new names to receiving light and sending signals.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the completed parts to make the eye felt a bit predictable after their positions had already been explained.

surprise.text: I learned that the retina is the light-sensitive lining and that its nerve fibres gather into the optic nerve.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though most choices after the first were the only offered combination rather than decisions I had to figure out.

continue.text: I might continue to see another body function built from parts; the pictures made this chapter understandable, although the mostly predictable combinations limited the challenge.
